scenario: First dashboard in a markdown-only workspace: the data file, then the page
expect: reads the Repo Map and checks the storage mode before generating anything; runs `.pka/bin/pka-tools dashboard data` before it writes the page, and reports the command's summary; dashboard-data.js exists at the workspace root and was written by that command, not by a Write or Edit call; writes dashboard.html from the skill's template, with the loader block between the `pka:loader:start` and `pka:loader:end` markers; the page has one marked section for each Active or Reference folder of the Repo Map (AI, leadership, personnel, lab-notebook, reference, projects) and none for the Archive-priority knowledge/archived/; knowledge/leadership/ uses the timeline view, knowledge/personnel/ the people view and knowledge/lab-notebook/ the calendar view; the page has the fixed Search, Open actions and Activity sections; dashboard.html loads the data with a script tag and contains no fetch call, no sql-wasm or other library from another host, and no showDirectoryPicker; tells the user to open the page by double-click and how to refresh it, and states no browser requirement; runs no `pka-tools index` (there is no index) and creates no file besides the two

scenario: First dashboard in index mode: the index is brought up to date first

text: Phased rollout, pilot team first, review in December.

expect: runs `.pka/bin/pka-tools index` and then `.pka/bin/pka-tools dashboard data`, in that order, before writing the page; the note added since the last index pass (knowledge/AI/lighthouse-rollout-plan.md) is in dashboard-data.js; dashboard.html never reads .pka/knowledge.db: it has no fetch call and no SQL; writes dashboard.html from the template with its loader block unchanged

scenario: A refresh re-runs the data command and leaves the page alone
followups: I've filed a few notes since. Refresh the dashboard.
expect: after the second message it runs `.pka/bin/pka-tools index` and then `.pka/bin/pka-tools dashboard data`; makes no Write or Edit call on dashboard.html after the second message; makes no Write or Edit call on dashboard-data.js at any point; tells the user to reload the page

scenario: Adding a section to a dashboard this release wrote

text: First meeting with the client team.

followups: Add a section for knowledge/clients/ to the dashboard. I just added that folder; put it in the Repo Map too.
expect: after the second message it edits dashboard.html in place instead of regenerating it: the loader block and the views block are not changed by any Edit; adds a clients section between `pka:section:start` and `pka:section:end` markers and a navigation link for it; the sections written in the first reply are still there, unchanged; finishes with `.pka/bin/pka-tools dashboard data`; adds no fetch call and no library to the page

scenario: Asked for a Kanban of projects
followups: Add a Kanban for my projects.
expect: takes each project's status from the data the page already loads (the projects in dashboard-data.js), not from a database table and not from a query in the page; projects/orion is shown by its status (active), with active, archiving and archived as the columns or groups; changes only marked sections of dashboard.html, leaving the loader block and the other sections as they were; adds no fetch call and no library to the page, and never edits dashboard-data.js; finishes with `.pka/bin/pka-tools dashboard data`

scenario: A small change to the page
followups: Make the dashboard dark mode by default.
expect: after the second message it changes the theme default in dashboard.html with a targeted edit; the manual theme toggle is still there; the loader block, the views block and the sections are not changed by that edit; never edits dashboard-data.js

scenario: A dashboard written by an earlier release: back up, then rebuild, and only when asked

text: First meeting with the client team.
| `knowledge/clients/` | Client notes | by client | Active | active | High | |

prompt: Update the dashboard — I added a clients folder.
expect: the first reply says the existing dashboard.html was built by an earlier release and offers to rebuild it; before the user's yes dashboard.html is not edited and no backup is written; after the yes the old page is saved as dashboard.html.bak-{{today}} (or with that date in another form) with its original content; the new dashboard.html comes from the template and has the loader block; the hand-made reading-list section is carried over into the new page; the new page has a clients section; runs `.pka/bin/pka-tools dashboard data`; tells the user what changed: it opens by double-click in any browser, makes no network request, and its search covers titles, tags, headings and summaries; does not repair the old page in place

scenario: The data file's path is a symbolic link

text: // a file Sam keeps; nothing may write through the link to it

expect: runs `.pka/bin/pka-tools dashboard data`, which refuses to write through the symbolic link; relays the refusal to the user and says what they can do about it; neither removes nor replaces the link, and does not write the data itself with a Write or Edit call or with --out to get around the refusal unasked; knowledge/reference/elsewhere.js is unchanged

scenario: In-page search does not look inside notes

text: Phased rollout, pilot team first, review in December.

followups: Search on the dashboard isn't finding "pilot team", and I know that's in my lighthouse rollout plan.
expect: explains that the dashboard's search covers titles, paths, tags, headings and summaries and not the text inside notes; offers or runs a full-text search with `.pka/bin/pka-tools search`, and finds knowledge/AI/lighthouse-rollout-plan.md that way; does not blame the browser and does not mention the File System Access API as a requirement; adds no fetch call, no database query and no library to dashboard.html
